claims.head: In close vs. from distance
claims.body: The Penguins get in close, but the Blue Jackets mostly shoot from distance. Pittsburgh is the league’s best for shots from in close, and Columbus is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Penguins to do more of their damage around the net.

PIT.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Pittsburgh has home-ice advantage. The Blue Jackets can make it interesting if they get good looks.

story.head: Somebody has to win
paras: The Blue Jackets won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in a shootout in Columbus on Oct 9. The Penguins (8-15-2) beat Buffalo 6-3 on Friday, while the Blue Jackets are winless in three (0-2-1). Both teams are near the bottom of the standings. This is a Metropolitan Division matchup, with the Jackets seventh (30th in the NHL) and the Penguins last (31st).

The Blue Jackets have played better than their record (.396) says: their chances are worth about .512, and their finishing has held them back. So have the Penguins (.360 on chances worth .531), mostly because they’re 4-8 in one-goal games.

The Blue Jackets get their defensemen shooting (2nd), lean on their stars as much as almost anyone (2nd most) and forecheck as hard as almost anyone (2nd). The Penguins, by contrast, sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (lowest). Columbus has scored 2.33 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Penguins rarely throw hits (lowest). The Penguins get in close, but the Blue Jackets mostly shoot from distance. Beyond that, the Penguins could find some good looks against the Blue Jackets, who give up plenty of them.

Kent Johnson (9 G / 14 A / 23 P in 24 GP) leads the Blue Jackets in scoring, and Zach Werenski (5 G / 16 A / 21 P in 24 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Penguins, Evgeni Malkin (8 G / 14 A / 22 P in 21 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Tommy Novak (9 G / 9 A / 18 P in 25 GP) has a team-high nine goals.
Cam Talbot (7-5-1 / .906 SV% in 13 GS) will likely start for Columbus, and Artūrs Šilovs (5-9-1 / .873 SV% in 15 GS) for Pittsburgh.
